summary: Pass for the Phase 4 security gate. The audited HEAD equals the branch tip and the working tree is clean. The diff holds 21 files: 13 manifests, one override line, the lockfile, two Measure documents and four test files. No application source, CI, workflow, secret or deploy file changed. The lockfile resolves next at 16.4.6 in every resolution and adds only the 10 next-family keys. The registry publishes 16.4.5 and 16.4.6, and the added integrity hashes match the registry. pnpm audit --prod reports critical 0 and the same 12 high advisories at HEAD and at the phase base. The full audit reports critical 0 and the same 16 high advisories at both. The moderate set at HEAD equals the base set minus exactly the two in-scope Next.js advisories. The audit reports zero next advisories at HEAD. The image-size ABSENT_BY_DESIGN row keeps its 2.0.3 floor for a copy that returns. The committed-evidence rewrite leaves every version floor checked against committed files. The eight phase-check failures are not upgrade defects: each cause is a source, fixture, build-output or environment issue. Nothing was pushed and origin holds no branch for security/next-16-4-6. Five nonblocking findings remain. The largest one is a stale follow-redirects guard floor that leaves one unclassified high advisory open at the phase base and at HEAD.
nonblocking_findings: NB-1: Unclassified high advisory at the phase base and at HEAD. follow-redirects@1.16.1 stays locked. npm audit reports one high finding for follow-redirects (id 1244003, vulnerable >=1.16.0 <=1.16.1, patched >=1.16.2). The guard floor of 1.16.1 at tests/security-upgrade-guard-list.ts:230 sits one patch below the fix, so the version-guard test stays green while the advisory is open. The plan sentence at task 2.14, "No unclassified high finding remains", is false at HEAD. The finding is identical at the phase base, so the Phase 4 diff neither caused nor closed it. Route: raise the follow-redirects floor to 1.16.2 or later and refresh the lockfile in a follow-up task. That widens the lockfile scope past the next family, so the PM owns the scope decision. Do not close the track on the task 2.14 claim.

NB-2: The recorded baseline-browser-mapping move left a vulnerable copy in the tree. The move from 2.10.38 to 2.11.33 applies to the next and browserslist snapshots only. apps/science-advantage/package.json:97 declares baseline-browser-mapping ^2.8.32 directly, and pnpm-lock.yaml:2057 still resolves that importer to 2.10.38. The moderate advisory for baseline-browser-mapping stays open at HEAD, exactly as at the phase base. The task 4.2 plan text records the move and does not claim that the advisory closed. Route: raise the science-advantage direct dependency or add an override in a follow-up task so the 2.10.38 copy leaves the tree.

NB-3: The base comparison worktree isolates source changes only. /home/daniebo/.cache/security-baseline-837755eaa links node_modules to the 16.4.6 worktree, so next resolves to 16.4.6 there. The eight predates-track reproductions compare base source against the new dependency versions. The comparison cannot by itself exclude a failure caused by the dependency bump. The eight enumerated causes are source, fixture, build-output or environment issues. The storytime failures read the absent gitignored file measure/runs/storytime_app_rebuild_20261025/media-list-w01.md, which is absent in the base copy too. The classification is credible, but the plan sentence "No failure is caused by 16.4.6" rests on the causes, not on the base runs. Route: qualify that sentence, or run one dependency-accurate base with next 16.4.1 installed.

NB-4: The committed-evidence rewrite lowers the CI-verifiable evidence for the Phase 2 matrix. A missing run log is now acceptable for all 73 ledger rows, including the 58 pass rows and the 13 predates-track master comparisons. The 73 rows stay pinned by LEDGER_ROW_FINGERPRINT. The two local-log checks still run in full when a log exists. No package version floor reads measure/runs, so no vulnerable package is hidden. The PM decision of 2026-11-18 authorizes the rewrite. Route: keep the rewrite, and record in the plan that a clean checkout cannot verify the exit_code labels of the 58 pass rows.

NB-5: The track registry row is stale. measure/tracks.md:54 still reads "Phase 1 (version guard and upgrade) next" while task 4.4 is closed. The row understates progress and claims no resolved security state, so A6 fires no overstatement. Route: refresh the status row, and add the Phase 4 scope plus the follow-redirects and baseline-browser-mapping follow-ups before the track closes.
